metadata.title: Comparative analysis of global education performances based on PISA 2022 results: an assessment with statistical and machine learning methods

design_fields.q1_rationale: The study does not use PISA student microdata; instead, it uses OECD-published country-level aggregated average scores, making plausible value handling not applicable.
design_fields.q2_rationale: The study explicitly states that it does not use PISA student microdata and therefore does not apply any sampling weights.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The study analyzes country-level aggregated data rather than student-level data, so school clustering is not applicable.
design_fields.q4_rationale: The study mentions using stratified k-fold cross-validation for internal validation, which does not qualify as validation beyond the estimation sample.
design_fields._pdf_matched: 195. Çelik et al. (2026). Comparative analysis of global education performances based on PISA 2022 results: an assessment with statistical and machine learning methods.pdf
design_fields.q4b_note: LLM (gpt-5.4-nano): It uses OECD-published PISA 2022 country-level average scores (one observation per country/economy) and applies correlations/PCA, regression (R²=1.0), and clustering with stratified 5-fold cross-validation; no separate per-country/system analyses are described.
